summary: These auto and semiconductor counterparties are linked by shared exposures to trade and geopolitics (tariffs, export controls, US-China tensions), supply-chain concentration (single-source suppliers, own-plant disruption), funding (credit ratings, leverage), tax changes, government incentive clawbacks, natural disasters, product cybersecurity, product liability and anti-corruption compliance. Each risk is shared by three to five of APTV, BWA, F, GM, LEA, MCHP, NXPI, ON, TSLA and TXN, as detailed in the claims.

raw_claims.quote: Compliance-related issues in certain countries associated with laws such as the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act and other anti-corruption laws could adversely affect our business.

Our failure to comply with anti-corruption laws could result in penalties that could harm our reputation and have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.
Our revolving credit agreement includes an increase in interest rates if the ratings for our debt are downgraded. The interest cost on our revolving credit agreement is based on a rating grid.

A downgrade of our credit rating by a major credit rating agency could result in increased borrowing costs and could adversely affect our ability to access the debt markets to refinance our existing debt or finance future debt.

Actual or anticipated changes or downgrades in our credit ratings, including any announcement that our ratings are under further review for a downgrade, could affect our market value and/or increase our corporate borrowing costs.
Many components used in our products are available only from a single or limited number of suppliers and, therefore, cannot be re-sourced quickly or inexpensively to another supplier
In some instances, we purchase systems, components, raw materials, and parts that are ultimately derived from a single source and may be at an increased risk for supply disruptions.
Any significant disruption in our supplier relationships, particularly relationships with sole-source suppliers, could harm our profitability.

Difficulties in the production process can reduce yields or interrupt production, and, as a result of such problems, we may on occasion not be able to deliver products or do so in a timely or cost-effective or competitive manner.

The impact of government incentives on Ford’s business has been and could continue to be significant, and Ford’s receipt of government incentives could be subject to reduction, termination, or clawback.

These programs are subject to periodic review by the relevant governments, and if any of these programs are curtailed or discontinued, this could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

A natural disaster that results in a prolonged disruption, particularly where we have principal manufacturing and design operations, as listed in the Properties section in Item 2, may adversely affect our results and financial condition.

In addition, increased intensity, frequency, or duration of storms, droughts, wildfires, or other severe weather events as a result of climate change may disrupt our production and the production, logistics, cost, and procurement of products from our suppliers
Failure of such products to effectively protect against attacks targeted at our products can negatively impact our brand and our business or results of operation.
Any unauthorized access to or control of our products or their systems or any loss of data could result in legal claims or government investigations.
Also, China presents unique risks to U.S. automotive manufacturers due to the strain in U.S.-China relations and the level of integration with key components in our global supply chain.
Licenses or license exceptions are often required for the shipment of our products to certain countries as well as for releases of our technology and software to foreign nationals.

As a result, the tax laws in the European Union, U.S. and other countries in which we and our affiliates do business could change on a prospective or retroactive basis, and any such changes could adversely affect us and our affiliates.
In addition, the occurrence of such defects may give rise to product liability and warranty claims, including liability for damages caused by such defects.

Credit rating downgrade and funding access
High leverage and debt service burden
Joint venture partner and control risk
AI adoption operational and legal risk
Armed conflict disrupting global supply chains
Climate and greenhouse gas regulation costs
New product launch and ramp delays
Physical climate and extreme weather disruption
